meta.revised: 2026-10-14 after review; see docs/data_profile.md section 10 (Review log): 20 findings accepted, 0 rejected; revised again after implementation review F1 (section 11): strict filing-date counts, 103(i) rule, E28 realisation, deterministic levels, temporal protocol

load.placeholder_note: src/mlda/data/load.py strips every column and masks the placeholder strings to NaN before any feature code runs. Every formula below therefore tests isna()/notna() or uses fillna('none'); a comparison with the literal '?' would evaluate False on NaN and invert flags (97,867 ones instead of 3,665 for immed_reportable). SHIFT_BEGIN_TIME has 48 three-character values (E10), so times are not uniformly zero-padded HHMM strings.
load.filing_date: DOCUMENT_NO[1:8] parsed as Julian YYYYDDD (18 of 275,220 rows unparsable); used for the filed-before-ACCIDENT_DT cut of the lagged case features

target.name: lost_time
target.label_meaning: indemnity-trigger label, not a severity label: codes 03/04 vs 05 depend on whether the operator offers restricted duty. Coal exceeds metal in 40 of 43 matched nature x body-part cells (median +19.0 pp); 05 share of DART cases ranges 0.4%-68.4% (p5-p95) across mines with >= 100 DART rows; COAL_METAL_IND Cramer's V 0.240 with this label vs 0.015 with the DART label. Valid for insurer/self-insured reserving and return-to-work planning; inspection targeting uses the DART sensitivity label. Report every metric stratified by COAL_METAL_IND.

label_validity.action: keep all 424 as positives on the MSHA degree code

sensitivity_labels.name: serious
sensitivity_labels.use: sensitivity analysis only; depends on right-censored DAYS_LOST

sensitivity_labels.name: dart
sensitivity_labels.use: sensitivity label for the inspection-targeting use; invariant to restricted-duty practice

fallback.name: serious
fallback.use: sensitivity analysis only; depends on right-censored DAYS_LOST

label_drift.note: overall prevalence 47.25%-50.13% by year is a composition artefact: coal prevalence rises monotonically while the coal share of rows falls
label_drift.mitigation: sector x year table in data_profile.md section 1; metrics and calibration by sector on the temporal split; CAL_YR or coal x year term is a candidate feature for the temporal variant only (extrapolation caveat)

row_filter_sequence.reason: partial year; label-incomplete: 46.97% of 03/04 rows lack DAYS_LOST; degree code provisional at filing (880 of 939 unresolved 2026 rows coded 03; Sep 2026 mix 03 53.9% / 04 1.7% / 05 8.6% / 06 33.1% vs 2025 38.5 / 9.8 / 21.4 / 28.5)

row_filter_sequence.caveat: 1,289 of the 07 rows have DAYS_LOST > 0 (2.54% of the lost-time population) and are out of scope; 816 accident-dated illness-nature rows remain in the base

row_filter_sequence.note: clean: 0 rows with DAYS_LOST > 0 or DAYS_RESTRICT > 0

completeness_check.method: quarter-level degree mix (shares of 03/04/05/06) against the same year's earlier quarters; the DAYS_LOST-missing test does not detect late re-coding
completeness_check.decision: keep 2025 Q4; about 5% of its rows (0.05% of the window) exposed to re-coding 9-12 months after the snapshot; documented in data_profile.md sections 2 and 9

dropped_after_review.COMPANY_TYPE: raw V = 0.044; dated version's Unknown level tracks accident age (41.2% of 2010 rows, 3.0% of 2025 rows, 0% at deployment)
dropped_after_review.CURRENT_CONTROLLER_BEGIN_DT: only needed for the dropped company_type_at_accident

prior_year_case_counts_from_full_acciden.filter: cases at the same MINE_ID with CAL_YR == row CAL_YR - 1 AND filing date (DOCUMENT_NO Julian) < row ACCIDENT_DT
prior_year_case_counts_from_full_acciden.valid: count of such rows with DEGREE_INJURY_CD in 01-06
prior_year_case_counts_from_full_acciden.lost_time: count of such rows with DEGREE_INJURY_CD in 01-04
prior_year_case_counts_from_full_acciden.strictness_evidence_note: implemented in review F1: base columns prev_incidents_resolved, prev_valid_cases_resolved, prev_lost_time_cases_resolved (30505 rows differ from the default) and prev_year_incomplete_at_filing (1643 rows filed by 15 January); sensitivity refits in sensitivity.json
prior_year_case_counts_from_full_acciden.strictness_evidence: 1.87% of t-1 cases filed after the row's ACCIDENT_DT (11.7% of rows with prior cases, 21.2% of Q1 rows); filed-before cut changes prev_lost_time_share for 7,743 rows, AUC 0.6708 vs 0.6710 for year totals; resolved-before variant (filing, RTW and closing document all before ACCIDENT_DT) changes 28,789 rows, AUC 0.668, kept as sensitivity variant only

production_prev_year.unmatched_action: keep rows, exposure features NaN, indicator kept as feature prev_year_matched

production_same_year_eda_only.use: EDA rates per 200,000 h and the EDA-only same-year mine type; never a model feature

type_at_time.source: set of production SUBUNIT_CD per MINE_ID x CALENDAR_YR at CAL_YR - 1 (same key as production_prev_year)
type_at_time.rule: if {01,02} intersect set -> Underground; elif set subset of {30,99,17} -> Facility; else Surface; if no t-1 production: fallback from accident SUBUNIT_CD (01/02 -> Underground; 30/99/17 -> Facility; else Surface)
type_at_time.why_not_same_year: 25.05% of accidents are in Q1 when no Form 7000-2 quarter of year t has been filed (30 CFR 50.30: 15 days after quarter end)

artefacts.grain: one row per Accidents case at base mines 2009-2025
artefacts.purpose: rebuild filed-before-ACCIDENT_DT lagged counts for any accident date

inference_lookup.fallback: manual entry of previous-year hours, employees and case counts in app/pages/5_Inference.py when the mine is not in the table

features.categorical_placeholder_handling: after load.py these columns hold NaN where the file had '?' / 'NO VALUE FOUND'; apply fillna('none') before OneHotEncoder so the structural placeholder stays one level (E13-E15); ACTIVITY_CD NaN (6 rows) also fillna('none') and falls into the infrequent bucket (E16)

engineered.name: accident_hour
engineered.formula: t = int(ACCIDENT_TIME); NaN if 9990<=t<=9999; 0 if t==2400; else t//100 when 0<=t<=2359 and t%100<60

engineered.name: shift_begin_hour
engineered.formula: same parsing as accident_hour applied to int(SHIFT_BEGIN_TIME) (48 three-character values parse as integers, E10; NaN after load.py masking -> NaN)

engineered.name: hours_into_shift
engineered.formula: acc_min = 60*hh+mm of ACCIDENT_TIME (2400->0); shift_min likewise; ((acc_min - shift_min) mod 1440)/60; NaN if either time invalid or result > 16

engineered.name: accident_weekday
engineered.formula: ACCIDENT_DT.weekday() (0=Monday)

engineered.name: is_weekend
engineered.formula: accident_weekday in {5,6}

engineered.name: accident_month
engineered.formula: ACCIDENT_DT.month

engineered.name: accident_quarter
engineered.formula: CAL_QTR (optional, redundant with month)

engineered.name: log1p_tot_exper
engineered.formula: log1p(TOT_EXPER)

engineered.name: exper_ratio_mine
engineered.formula: NaN if MINE_EXPER or TOT_EXPER is NaN or TOT_EXPER <= 0 else clip(MINE_EXPER / TOT_EXPER, 0, 1), after error rules E1-E3 (E30 guard: 0 zero denominators in the base, min TOT_EXPER 0.02)

engineered.name: exper_ratio_job
engineered.formula: NaN if JOB_EXPER or TOT_EXPER is NaN or TOT_EXPER <= 0 else clip(JOB_EXPER / TOT_EXPER, 0, 1), after error rules E1-E3

engineered.name: new_to_mine
engineered.formula: MINE_EXPER < 1

engineered.name: exper_inconsistent
engineered.formula: 1 if JOB_EXPER > TOT_EXPER or MINE_EXPER > TOT_EXPER (before NaN-ing) else 0

engineered.name: is_contractor
engineered.formula: CONTRACTOR_ID.notna() (blank is masked to NaN by load.py)

engineered.name: immed_reportable
engineered.formula: IMMED_NOTIFY_CD.notna() & (IMMED_NOTIFY_CD != '13'); placeholders '? ' arrive as NaN from load.py; code 13 'Not marked' (77 rows, 2010-2012 only) -> 0 (E29); never use the raw code (01 = death)
engineered.caveat: 560 flagged rows are code 01 death and 100% positive (69.79% positive without them); report metrics with and without

engineered.name: no_injuries_capped
engineered.formula: min(NO_INJURIES, 10)

engineered.name: underground
engineered.formula: SUBUNIT_CD == '01' (optional, redundant with one-hot)

engineered.name: type_at_time
engineered.formula: see join.type_at_time (t-1 subunit set, SUBUNIT_CD fallback)

engineered.name: prev_hours
engineered.formula: sum ANNUAL_HRS at (MINE_ID, CAL_YR-1)

engineered.name: prev_employees
engineered.formula: sum AVG_ANNUAL_EMPL at (MINE_ID, CAL_YR-1)

engineered.name: prev_hours_per_employee
engineered.formula: prev_hours / prev_employees (NaN if employees == 0)

engineered.name: log1p_prev_hours
engineered.formula: log1p(prev_hours)

engineered.name: mine_size_band
engineered.note: left-closed bins; 2,211 matched rows sit exactly on 5/20/50/200 and change band under the pandas default right=True

engineered.name: prev_incidents
engineered.formula: count of Accidents rows (any code) at (MINE_ID, CAL_YR-1) with filing date < ACCIDENT_DT; 0 if t-1 production exists but no such case; NaN if no t-1 production
engineered.true_zeros_note: strict filing_date < ACCIDENT_DT; a <= cut gives 17820 (272 (row, case) pairs are filed on the accident date)

engineered.name: prev_incident_rate_200k
engineered.formula: log1p(min(prev_incidents / prev_hours * 200000, 50))

engineered.name: prev_lost_time_rate_200k
engineered.formula: log1p(min(prev_lost_time_cases / prev_hours * 200000, 50)) where prev_lost_time_cases = count of codes 01-04 at t-1 filed before ACCIDENT_DT

engineered.name: prev_lost_time_share
engineered.formula: prev_lost_time_cases / prev_valid_cases (codes 01-06 at t-1 filed before ACCIDENT_DT); NaN if prev_valid_cases == 0
engineered.rows_available_note: strict filing_date < ACCIDENT_DT; the earlier <= cut gave 81525 present (20084 missing)

engineered.name: prev_year_matched
engineered.formula: _m_prev == 'both'

engineered.name: ytd_lost_time_share
engineered.formula: lost-time share of same-MINE_ID cases with CAL_YR == row CAL_YR, codes 01-06, filing date < ACCIDENT_DT; NaN if none
engineered.note: explicit time-safe form of same-year mine history; the only permitted route for it (see split)

engineered.name: status_103i_at_accident
engineered.formula: 'Never had 103I' if CURRENT_103I == 'Never Had 103I Status'; elif CURRENT_103I is present and CURRENT_103I_DT <= ACCIDENT_DT: ('Formerly 103I' if CURRENT_103I == 'Removed From 103I Status' else 'In 103I at accident'); else 'Unknown' (any status dated after the accident, 'Removed From 103I Status' included, or blank). Review F1: the former branch that sent removed-after rows to 'In 103I at accident' used a fact dated a median 4.3 years after the accident and an unknown placement date
engineered.caveat: Unknown mixes later-dated and blank statuses in training (24.1% of 2010-2019 rows, 16.9% of 2020-2025 rows) but only blank statuses at deployment; metrics with and without the feature are reported on the primary and the temporal split (sensitivity.json, temporal_split.json); dropping the feature from FEATURE_SPEC would change interfaces.md section 3; the without-feature refits differ by less than 0.001 AUC

engineered.name: latitude
engineered.formula: LATITUDE if 17.5<=lat<=72 and -180<=lon<=-64 (or STATE == 'AS') else NaN

engineered.name: longitude
engineered.formula: LONGITUDE under the same validity rule

engineered_removed_after_review.name: company_type_at_accident
engineered_removed_after_review.reason: Unknown level encodes accident age (41.2% of 2010 rows -> 3.0% of 2025 rows; 34.4% vs 8.0% across the temporal split; 0% at deployment); raw COMPANY_TYPE Cramer's V 0.044; lost-time gap is commodity composition

not_features: CAL_YR (filter and temporal split; candidate feature for the temporal-split variant only, because of the within-coal label drift, with an extrapolation caveat)

level_drift_inside_window.OCCUPATION: code list revised around 2014-01-31; 'Discontinued 1/31/2014. Several other codes cover Scoop Car Operator' (code 054, 533 rows, 2010-2014) -> infrequent bucket (E28); 7 titles with >= 100 rows first appear 2013-2014
level_drift_inside_window.EQUIP_MFR_NAME: 7 names with >= 100 rows first appear 2013-2014 (Volvo 313, Sandvik 202, DeWalt 177, Milwaukee 146, Peterbilt 131, Bobcat 130, JLG 119)
level_drift_inside_window.check: temporal split: report one-hot columns that are all-zero in the test period

one_hot.note: 0.1% of rows = about 100 on the full window, about 81 on the 80% training split; estimated width about 504 columns (468 accident levels + 13 infrequent buckets + 23 mine/derived levels)

drop_admin_note: raw columns consumed by an engineered feature (ACCIDENT_TIME, SHIFT_BEGIN_TIME, CONTRACTOR_ID, IMMED_NOTIFY_CD, CURRENT_103I, CURRENT_103I_DT, LATITUDE, LONGITUDE, CAL_QTR) are dropped after derivation; COMPANY_TYPE and CURRENT_CONTROLLER_BEGIN_DT are dropped outright (see drop_leakage)

error_rules.name: E7_accident_time_other_invalid
error_rules.condition: ACCIDENT_TIME blank, minutes >= 60 or > 2400 outside codes

error_rules.name: E8_shift_time_code_or_blank
error_rules.condition: 9990 <= SHIFT_BEGIN_TIME <= 9999 or NaN (blank masked by load.py)

error_rules.name: E10_shift_time_short
error_rules.action: parse as integer HHMM (700 -> 07:00); do not string-slice

error_rules.name: E13_ug_location_placeholder
error_rules.action: fillna('none'); keep as level (structural: 0 in subunit 01)

error_rules.name: E14_ug_method_placeholder
error_rules.action: fillna('none'); keep as level (927 genuinely missing in subunit 01)

error_rules.name: E16_activity_placeholder
error_rules.action: fillna('none'); falls into the infrequent bucket

error_rules.name: E18_equip_mfr_code_series
error_rules.condition: EQUIP_MFR_CD 3-digit and 4-digit codes for one name

error_rules.name: E19_occupation_sector_prefix
error_rules.condition: OCCUPATION_CD sector prefixes for one title

error_rules.name: E22_dates
error_rules.condition: ACCIDENT_DT unparsable or after snapshot; CAL_YR/CAL_QTR != derived

error_rules.name: E24_mine_attr_not_in_force
error_rules.condition: CURRENT_103I_DT > ACCIDENT_DT and not 'Never Had'; (CURRENT_CONTROLLER_BEGIN_DT > ACCIDENT_DT)
error_rules.action: 103I: any status dated after the accident ('Removed From 103I Status' included, 8,091 rows) or blank -> 'Unknown' (22,368 rows, 22.01%); COMPANY_TYPE: feature dropped

error_rules.name: E25_unstable_rates
error_rules.action: winsorise rates at 50 per 200k h then log1p; keep raw counts

error_rules.name: E28_discontinued_occupation
error_rules.action: map to the 'missing' level of OCCUPATION (successor codes not identified in the codebook); a stateless step cannot reach the one-hot infrequent bucket because 533 rows (0.66%) exceed min_frequency, so the level becomes the one-hot column OCCUPATION_missing, non-zero in 2010-2014 only and reported in temporal_split.json level_drift (e28_retired_occupation_column_all_zero)

error_rules.name: E30_zero_denominator
error_rules.condition: TOT_EXPER <= 0 or NaN in exper_ratio_mine / exper_ratio_job

numeric_imputer.why_no_add_indicator: prev_hours, prev_employees, prev_hours_per_employee, prev_incidents and both rates are missing on exactly the same 1,206 rows, so add_indicator would emit six copies of 1 - prev_year_matched plus duplicates of prev_share_missing and TOT_EXPER_missing (KNN distance inflation, collinearity for LogReg)

duplicates.action: keep all rows (one form per injured person)

group_key_nested: MINE_ID + '_' + ACCIDENT_DT (multi-victim key; every same-day group lies inside one mine-year)

split.method: StratifiedGroupKFold(n_splits=5, shuffle=True, random_state=42) on mine-year groups; one fold held out as test
split.cv: StratifiedGroupKFold(n_splits=5, shuffle=True, random_state=42) on the training 80%, same mine-year groups
split.stratification_check: unstratified random assignment of mine-years to 5 folds gives fold prevalence 46.47%-50.92%; StratifiedGroupKFold keeps each split within 1 pp of 48.6%
tests: no group_id in both train and test
class share within 1 pp of 48.585% in each split
no nested MINE_ID + ACCIDENT_DT group split across sets

temporal_split.role: reported side by side with the primary split for S1-S6; carries the level-drift and label-drift checks; metrics and calibration by sector; with and without status_103i_at_accident

robustness_variants_implemented.group by MINE_ID: mlda.sensitivity.mine_grouped_robustness -> reports/metrics/sensitivity.json mine_grouped_split and success_criteria.json robustness_mine_grouped_split

split.temporal_protocol: the primary protocol repeated on CAL_YR 2010-2019: every model re-tuned with the same grids and grouped CV, the two best by pre-2020 cross-validated average precision kept, thresholds from pre-2020 out-of-fold probabilities, 2020-2025 labels used only for the final scores (79.5% of the 2020-2025 rows are training rows of the primary split, so primary-split thresholds, grid choices or rankings would carry their labels)

known_deterministic_levels.label: AMPUTATION OR ENUCLEATION
known_deterministic_levels.decision: kept: definitional (an amputation is a permanent impairment) and known at filing, but deterministic
known_deterministic_levels.reporting: held-out metrics with and without these rows at the fixed thresholds (reports/metrics/sensitivity.json excluding_pure_levels)
known_deterministic_levels.guard: tests/test_leakage.py asserts that the set of levels with at least 100 rows that are 100% one class equals {NATURE_INJURY_CD=100}

cost.note: C_FN and the 20:1 base ratio are assumptions: 5-10% of the NCCI AY2025 average lost-time claim (USD 61.9k) is a judgement, not a cited share, and the NCCI report-lag study (13,210 -> 17,785 -> 19,936 USD) is an analogy about late reporting to the insurer, whereas every case here is already filed with MSHA within 10 working days; the anchors mix a 2015 all-claim median with a 2025 lost-time mean
cost.non_trivial_threshold_region: ratio <= about 5:1 (p* >= 0.167): no nature/body-part/source level with n >= 100 has a lost-time rate below 0.079; 0 rows in nature x body-part x coal cells (n >= 100) below 0.0476 and 1,087 rows (1.07%) below 0.0909; at >= 10:1 a calibrated model flags every case
cost.beat_floor_condition: (1 - recall) < ((1 - prevalence) / (prevalence * ratio)) * specificity; = 0.529 / 0.353 / 0.212 / 0.106 / 0.053 / 0.035 x specificity at 2 / 3 / 5 / 10 / 20 / 30 : 1

lookup_nature_bodypart_coal.rule: cell lost-time rate of NATURE_INJURY_CD x INJ_BODY_PART_CD x COAL_METAL_IND fitted on train; unseen cells fall back to nature x coal, then nature

success_criteria.evaluation_set: 20% mine-year-grouped held-out test set; CV mean +/- std and the temporal split (train 2010-2019, test 2020-2025) reported alongside; every metric also stratified by COAL_METAL_IND
success_criteria.operating_point: capacity operating point: threshold chosen on out-of-fold probabilities so that specificity = 0.40 (flag rate about 75%, the review-capacity assumption); decoupled from the cost ratio because at >= 10:1 the cost-optimal threshold flags every case

cost_criterion.definition: expected cost per 1,000 cases at the cost-optimal out-of-fold threshold, for each ratio in cost.ratio_sensitivity
cost_criterion.pass_rule: below the all-positive floor (102,829 on the full window; recomputed on the test set) AND below the 3-field lookup's cost-optimal cost at the same ratio (temporal holdout 76,860 / 87,677 / 97,437; recomputed on the test set)
cost_criterion.report_only_note: the all-positive floor is the optimum at >= 10:1, so only the distance to the floor is reported; the former rule 'below the best hand rule at 10/20/30:1' (142,417 / 212,174 / 281,932) was passed by the all-positive rule and is dropped

success_criteria.brier_note: overall and within each sector on the temporal split
statistical_tests: paired test across CV folds between top two models
additional_reporting: metrics with and without immed_reportable (sensitivity.json primary_split_variants, temporal_split.json)
metrics with and without status_103i_at_accident on the primary and the temporal split
held-out metrics with and without the rows of deterministic levels (sensitivity.json excluding_pure_levels; known_deterministic_levels)
resolved-before lag counts and blanked early-January exposure refits (sensitivity.json primary_split_variants)
bootstrap intervals and McNemar tests clustered by mine-year, beside the row-wise versions (statistical_tests.json)
optional: metrics for rows with RETURN_TO_WORK_DT <= filing date (44.96%, positive rate 20.35%) vs after (71.64%)
one-hot columns all-zero in the temporal test period (level drift)
